readme:
# lil agents for Windows

![lil agents](hero-thumbnail.png)

Tiny AI companions that live on your Windows taskbar.

**Bruce** and **Jazz** walk back and forth above your taskbar. Click one to open an AI terminal. They walk, they think, they vibe.

Supports **Claude Code**, **OpenAI Codex**, **GitHub Copilot**, and **Google Gemini** CLIs — switch between them from the system tray.

> **Note**: This is a native Windows WPF port of the original **[lil agents](https://lilagents.xyz)** project for macOS created by [Ryan Stephen](https://github.com/ryanstephen). The original source code can be found at the [lil-agents GitHub repository](https://github.com/ryanstephen/lil-agents).

## features

- Animated characters rendered from transparent sprite sheets
- Click a character to chat with AI in a themed popover terminal
- Switch between Claude, Codex, Copilot, and Gemini from the system tray menu
- Four visual themes: Peach, Midnight, Cloud, Moss
- Slash commands: `/clear`, `/copy`, `/help` in the chat input
- Copy last response button in the title bar
- Thinking bubbles with playful phrases while your agent works
- Sound effects on completion
- First-run onboarding with a friendly welcome

## requirements

- Windows 10 or Windows 11
- .NET 8.0 SDK (for building and running)
- At least one supported CLI installed:
  - [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/download) — `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`
  - [OpenAI Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) — `npm install -g @openai/codex`
  - [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli) — `npm install -g @githubnext/github-copilot-cli`
  - [Google Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) — `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli`

## building

Open the `LilAgents.Windows.sln` in Visual Studio or run from the command line using the .NET SDK:

```bash
cd LilAgents.Windows
dotnet run
```

## privacy

lil agents runs entirely on your PC and sends no personal data anywhere.

- **Your data stays local.** The app plays bundled animations and calculates your taskbar size to position the characters. No project data, file paths, or personal information is collected or transmitted.
- **AI providers.** Conversations are handled entirely by the CLI process you choose (Claude, Codex, Copilot, or Gemini) running locally. lil agents does not intercept, store, or transmit your chat content. Any data sent to the provider is governed by their respective terms and privacy policies.
- **No accounts.** No login, no user database, no analytics in the app.

files.summary: The .gitignore file specifies which files and directories should be ignored by Git when tracking changes in a project. It includes rules for ignoring files generated by various development tools like Visual Studio, Mono, NUnit, and others, as well as user-specific files, build artifacts, and temporary files. This helps maintain a clean repository by excluding unnecessary and potentially sensitive data.

The provided XAML code defines the application-wide resources, including a custom style for buttons that sets their background to transparent, removes border thickness, sets cursor to hand, and applies specific hover and pressed effects. This style is applied globally to all button elements within the application.

The provided C# code defines an application entry point for a Windows desktop app that operates solely from the system tray, without a main window. It initializes a `LilAgentsController` instance upon startup and handles exceptions during initialization by displaying a message box with error details before shutting down. Upon exit, it disposes of the controller instance.

The AssemblyInfo.cs file contains metadata for an assembly, specifying the location of theme-specific and generic resource dictionaries. This configuration allows the application to locate resources such as styles, brushes, and templates during runtime.

The CLAUDE.md file outlines how to build and understand the architecture of a macOS AppKit application called LilAgents. It details the central components such as the controller, character classes, session protocols, environment resolver, terminal view, and theming. The application features animated characters interacting with AI CLI tools through a GUI, utilizing various session types and customizable configurations per character.

The provided XAML code defines a transparent, topmost, non-resizable window named CharacterWindow for displaying character images in the LilAgents application. The window has a fixed size of 80x100 pixels and centers the character image horizontally and vertically at the bottom using an Image element with a ScaleTransform to allow flipping if needed.

The CharacterWindow class is a WPF window that hosts a transparent character sprite, allowing for interactive click events. It manages the window's properties such as size, position, and frame display, and provides methods to set the character's frame, size, origin, and position. The window also includes a hook for handling Windows messages to ensure proper interaction with the underlying system.

The SpriteAnimator class is a sprite-based animation engine that pre-loads PNG frames into memory for seamless frame switching, falling back to procedurally generated placeholder frames if PNGs are not available. It provides methods to load frames from directories or embedded resources and supports events for frame changes. The class also includes properties for current frame, total frame count, and an event for frame changes.

The WalkerCharacter class is a character controller for a game or simulation, implementing movement, popover, bubble, and session logic. It includes properties for video dimensions, duration, random phrases, and sound effects. The class manages various UI elements like windows, animators, and terminal views, and handles walk states, including start time, position progress, direction, and pause status. It also provides methods for playing sound effects and displaying popovers or bubbles.

The `AppSettings` class in the `LilAgents.Windows.Core` namespace is a sealed class that manages application settings for a Windows application. It uses an internal `AppSettingsData` class to store settings such as completion of onboarding, selected theme, sounds enablement, pinned display index, character visibility, providers, and sizes. The `AppSettings` class provides properties and methods to read and write these settings from and to a JSON file specified by `_filePath`. Key functionalities include retrieving and setting character providers and sizes, checking and modifying character visibility, and saving the settings to the JSON file.

summary: The lil-agents-win project creates tiny AI companions, named Bruce and Jazz, that reside on the Windows taskbar. These animated characters serve as conversational partners, offering users access to various AI models such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Google Gemini via their system tray menu. Users click on a character to engage in chat within a themed popover terminal, and they can utilize slash commands like /clear, /copy, and /help. The application supports four visual themes and includes sound effects and thinking bubbles for added engagement. It's designed for Windows 10 or 11 users who want a fun, interactive way to interact with AI models without sharing any personal data.
architecture:
1. The Lil Agents Win project is structured around a clear separation of concerns, with distinct folders for Core, Characters, Resources, and a top-level App directory containing the main application entry points. This modular design facilitates maintenance, scalability, and collaboration among team members.

   The Core folder houses essential application logic, such as app settings, the main controller (LilAgentsController), and environment management (ShellEnvironment). TaskbarDetector, a utility class for detecting taskbar visibility, is also located here. These components work together to manage the application's state and behavior across various environments.

   In the Characters folder, you'll find classes responsible for character representation and animation, including SpriteAnimator and WalkerCharacter. Character-related UI elements are defined in CharacterWindow.xaml and its associated code-behind (CharacterWindow.xaml.cs). This separation allows for easy updates and expansions of character models without affecting core application logic.

   Resources contain media assets like icons and sound effects, organized into subdirectories for better asset management.

2. Interaction between components occurs primarily through well-defined interfaces and dependencies. For instance, the LilAgentsController manages the overall application flow, interacting with ShellEnvironment to handle environment-specific behaviors and TaskbarDetector for taskbar visibility checks. CharacterWindow communicates with SpriteAnimator and WalkerCharacter to render and animate characters appropriately.

   The use of XAML for defining UIs and C# for implementing business logic enables a clean separation of presentation and logic. This approach allows developers to modify the user interface independently of the underlying functionality, promoting maintainability and reusability.

3. The project employs several architectural patterns, most notably Model-View-ViewModel (MVVM) for handling UI interactions and data binding. The View (XAML files) defines the UI layout, while the ViewModel (C# classes) holds presentation logic and data. The Model (business objects) encapsulates application data and logic.

   Additionally, the Singleton pattern is utilized for global configuration and state management, exemplified by the AppSettings class. Lastly, the Observer pattern can be inferred from the relationship between TaskbarDetector and other components that may need to react to changes in taskbar visibility.
